findings.rationale: The jump security group exposes TCP port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0, placing the administrative shell directly on the internet.
The escalation role trusts the wildcard principal and is attached to a policy that permits sts:AssumeRole, making it assumable by any suitable identity.
The connectivity graph links the internet-exposed jump security group to role-escalate through an sts:AssumeRole edge, forming an external-to-identity attack path.
The wildcard identity policy is chained to an S3 bucket with a public-read ACL, allowing an unbounded identity to reach publicly readable storage.
